resolutions.what_changed: The case now grades the call site as well as the ruling. `_main_exit_code(wall_seconds)` drives the real `evals.run.main()` with `load_cases` and `run_case` stubbed to a single result of a chosen duration — no case runs, no report is written, stdout and stderr are swallowed — and the case asserts the exit code: 0 for 54.35s, 1 for 79.02s. That is the code path `.github/workflows/eval.yml` and `.githooks/pre-commit` actually take, so the five-line block in `main()` can no longer be deleted with the suite green.
resolutions.watched_red: The `if over_budget(args.suite, totals["wall_seconds"]):` block deleted from evals/run.py (lines 166-170) and nothing else touched, with the extended case in the suite: `[FAIL] fast-wall-clock-budget`, 89/90 = 0.989 against baseline 1.000. `wrong: [{"wall_seconds": 79.02, "exit": 1, "got": 0}]` — the under-budget row still returned 0, so the case fails on the run that should have been stopped and not on the one that should not. Block restored: 90/90 = 1.000.
resolutions.bounded: No framework: one 20-line helper and two rows in the case file. No source-text inspection — the exit code is the thing that matters and the thing CI reads.

resolutions.what_changed: README.md's `it is 96 cases (86 of them in the offline gate)` reads `100 cases (90 of them in the offline gate)`. Ground truth: `ls evals/golden/*.json evals/adversarial/*.json` is 100 (20 + 80), and the committed fast report has 90 results.

The sentence no longer attributes the 86 -> 90 move to three cases. It now names all four: `fast-wall-clock-budget`, `agent-launches-its-own-browser` and `shared-browser-relaunches-when-dead` from M12 (the last two written in review), plus `adr-header-and-index` from the decision-first ADR retrofit that landed between M8 and M12. The fourth was identified rather than guessed: the ids in `evals/report/20260820-020212-fast.json` differenced against the `fast`-tagged cases at `main` give exactly `adr-header-and-index`.

Two changes, because the row table could only ever cover suite names someone thought to list. A `{"suite": "full", "wall_seconds": 999.0, "over": false}` row was added, AND the case now asserts `sorted(WALL_BUDGET_S) == expect.suites_with_a_ceiling` — a set comparison, so any future suite name added to the ruling turns it red whether or not a row exists for it.
resolutions.watched_red: The reviewer's exact mutation, in process: with `evals.run.WALL_BUDGET_S['full'] = 1`, `run_case(case)['passed']` was `True` before and is now `False`, failing twice over — `{'suite': 'full', 'wall_seconds': 999.0, 'over': False}` from the row and `{'ruling': 'suites', 'budgets': ['fast', 'full'], 'declared': ['fast']}` from the set check.
